s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative infection of a medical device implant site
salient_findings: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
Growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from the lesion swab
key_facts: 72-year-old man with no prior medical history
Underwent dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
Procedure was for 2:1 atrioventricular block
Procedure was uneventful
Discharged on postoperative day 1
Presented with fever (38.1°C) on postoperative day 4
Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site on postoperative day 4
Elevated inflammatory syndrome on laboratory studies
Blood cultures were obtained on postoperative day 4
Antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
Lesion darkened and enlarged by postoperative day 7
Blood cultures remained negative by postoperative day 7

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket infection
shortlist.why_kept: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site and positive swab culture for Staphylococcus epidermidis

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal biofilm infection
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Staphylococcus epidermidis and signs of infection despite antibiotic therapy

shortlist.label: Surgical site infection
shortlist.why_kept: Postoperative fever and inflamed lesion at the implant site

shortlist.label: Device-related endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a medical device and signs of infection

shortlist.label: Staphylococcus epidermidis bacteremia
shortlist.why_kept: Positive swab culture for Staphylococcus epidermidis and signs of systemic infection

raw.rationale: The patient presented with an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the pacemaker implant site, and a swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, which is consistent with a pacemaker pocket infection.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal biofilm infection
rejected.why: While Staphylococcus epidermidis is a common cause of biofilm infections, the presentation of a localized lesion over the implant site is more consistent with a pocket infection.

rejected.label: Surgical site infection
rejected.why: This is a broad term that could apply, but the specific involvement of the pacemaker pocket and the growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis make pacemaker pocket infection a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Device-related endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of valve involvement or other signs of endocarditis, such as heart murmur or embolic phenomena, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Staphylococcus epidermidis bacteremia
rejected.why: Blood cultures remained negative, which argues against bacteremia.
